evals.name: new-skill-from-docs
evals.prompt: our team uses an internal cli called tidyctl to clean up stale cloud resources, the docs are in docs/tidyctl.md. agents keep misusing it (deleting stuff they shouldnt, using the wrong config file etc). can you write an agent skill for it that works in both claude code and codex? put it under skills/
evals.expected_output: A skill under skills/ for tidyctl that leads an agent to plan before pruning, respect keep tags, use the right config file and recover from a partial run correctly.
assertions: check-skill.mjs reports no errors for the skill directory written or fixed
The frontmatter holds only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata or allowed-tools, so claude.ai, Claude Code and Codex all accept it
The description says what the skill does in the third person, then when to use it
The skill names nothing outside its own directory: no absolute paths, no links that leave it
It says prune deletes immediately and has no --dry-run, and to run plan first
It says keep=true tags are skipped only with --respect-tags or respect_tags = true
It names .tidyrc.toml as the config file, and that tidy.toml is ignored
It says --older-than takes whole days (14, not 14d)
It says exit 3 means resume <run-id>, never a second prune
It says to use TIDY_TOKEN and never --token
It holds no tool-invocation details irrelevant to tidyctl, such as generic explanations of what cloud resources are

evals.name: fix-broken-skill
evals.prompt: claude.ai refuses to upload skills/pdf-helper (some error about unexpected keys) and claude code never picks it up on its own unless I type /pdf-helper. please fix it so it works in claude.ai, claude code and codex.
evals.expected_output: skills/pdf-helper (or a renamed directory matching its name) that check-skill accepts, loads implicitly in Claude Code, uploads to claude.ai, and keeps every piece of the original guidance reachable.
assertions: check-skill.mjs reports no errors for the skill directory written or fixed
The frontmatter holds only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata or allowed-tools, so claude.ai, Claude Code and Codex all accept it
The description says what the skill does in the third person, then when to use it
The skill names nothing outside its own directory: no absolute paths, no links that leave it
name is lowercase-hyphenated and matches its directory
disable-model-invocation is removed, so the skill can load on its own
version and tags are removed or moved under metadata as strings
The form-field guidance from shared/forms.md is brought inside the skill, not linked outside it
references/details.md is linked from SKILL.md directly, or its content merged so nothing is nested
The date-bound PyPDF2/pypdf guidance is replaced with current guidance (pypdf)
scripts/fill.py is referenced with forward slashes

evals.name: skill-from-corrections
evals.prompt: I keep correcting agents about how we release acme-widgets. notes/turns.jsonl has the things I said to them over the last few weeks (one JSON object per line, with what the agent said just before). Turn it into a skill so I stop having to repeat myself.
evals.expected_output: A release skill for acme-widgets carrying each of the person's corrections as an instruction with its reason.
assertions: check-skill.mjs reports no errors for the skill directory written or fixed
The frontmatter holds only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata or allowed-tools, so claude.ai, Claude Code and Codex all accept it
The description says what the skill does in the third person, then when to use it
The skill names nothing outside its own directory: no absolute paths, no links that leave it
It says never to npm publish by hand: CI publishes on merging the release PR
It says never to squash: the changelog comes from the individual commits
It says to run pnpm install and commit pnpm-lock.yaml in the same commit as a dependency change
It types commits by what users see (--help fix is fix, README typo is docs)
It says to verify with npm view, provenance included, and to allow for registry lag
It says packages stay on 0.x until the API review
It says never to tag by hand or edit CHANGELOG.md by hand
It says to run just release-check before merging a release PR
It says packages/legacy-widgets must be removed from the release config
It does not paste the transcript in wholesale
